items.title: Akiyoshi Toshiko — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I started to play Storyville in ‟56... the main group was from Tuesday to Sunday... I should have a horn player, so there was Boots Mussulli... It was very good for me that he was there.

ctx.x: When we left off yesterday, we were talking about, you had just finished your tenure at Berklee School, and you were now going to launch your professional career. But, you know, you did talk about that you were already performing in Boston and also in New York … you played at Storyville?

Uh, Storyville, I started to play Storyville in ‟56, March, from Thursday to Sunday. And uh, in those days, most clubs had two groups. So the main group from … both in a seven nights‟ term, plus a matinee. So, but shorter hours than in New York: New York, those days, was 10 to 4, and Boston was 9 to 1, and seven nights, plus the matinee Sunday afternoon. So, um, I started to play, but the main group was from Tuesday to Sunday. And uh, that was very good for me, because I could hear also … um, the school thought—I…
